1. What is Python: a snake or something else?

Stage I · Programming and Setup Lesson 1

What comes to your mind when you hear the word Python? A big snake? Of course, a python is a large snake. But in the world of computers, Python is a fomous programming language. Python is a programming language created to make programs easier to read, write, and understand. Its design gives importance to clarity and simplicity.

A Small History of Python

Interestingly,the programming language was not actually named after the snake. Its creator, Guido van Rossum, named it after the British comedy programme Monty Python’s Flying Circus. He wanted a name that was short, memorable, and slightly playful.

Python was created by the Dutch programmer Guido van Rossum. He began developing it during the late 1980s while working at the Centre for Mathematics and Computer Science in the Netherlands. The first public version of Python was released in 1991. Guido wanted to create a programming language that was powerful but still easy to read. He believed that computer instructions should not look unnecessarily complicated. This focus on readability later became one of Python’s greatest strengths.

Programming Languages

1.1 Language vs programming language?

Before we begin : You have probably heard people say, “Learn a programming language,” “Python is easy,” or “Programming is the future.” But what exactly is a programming language? Why does a computer need a language? And among so many available languages, why are we beginning with Python?

1.1 Language vs programming language?

Why python is called as a language? In broader sense why is it called programming languages? Why not programming tool? programming method? For that we need to recall what is a common language. Common language is structured method of communication. It uses agreed words, sounds, symbols, and rules to transfer information from one person to another. Blind people uses brelly and sign languages. Some times we meet different linguistic people, we don't know how to speak, in that case if we can able to give some hand gesture or body gesture to make the front person understand our need. That is the way of communication and that is also a kind of language.

Early computers can't understand normal English or body gestures. They only knew their languange to comunicate. They could only read 0 and 1. No doubt today's computer can understand much better. But they can understand normal convesation they are trained for. If you want something complicated and you give english instruction, then it can't understand it. It can understand syntaxs and designatated language called Programming language.

Defination:Programing language lets humans communicate instructions to computers.

1.2 Types of Computer Languages

Computer languages have developed over time to make communication with computers easier. The closer a language is to the computer's hardware, the more difficult it is for humans to read. The closer it is to human language, the easier it is for people to write and understand.

Computer languages can be broadly divided into two main groups:

  1. Low-level languages
  2. High-level languages
Remember: “Low-level” does not mean unimportant or poor quality. It means that the language works close to the computer's hardware. Similarly, “high-level” means that the language is closer to human-readable ideas.

1.2.1 Low-Level Languages

A low-level language provides instructions that are very close to the computer's hardware. These languages give programmers more direct control over the processor and memory.

Low-level languages are usually more difficult for humans to read, write, debug, and maintain. They may also depend on the particular processor or computer architecture being used.

Low-level languages are divided into two main types:

  • Machine language
  • Assembly language

1.2.2 Machine-Level Language

Machine language, also called machine code, is the lowest-level computer language. It consists of instructions represented using binary digits: 0 and 1.

A machine-language instruction may look like this: 

10110000 01100001

To a beginner, this looks like a random collection of zeros and ones. However, to a particular processor, the sequence may represent an operation such as moving data, adding values, or comparing two values.

Machine language can be executed directly by the computer's processor. It does not need to be translated into another language before execution.

✓

Directly Executable

The processor can execute machine-language instructions directly.

✓

Fast and Hardware-Specific

The instructions are designed for a particular processor architecture.

!

Difficult to Read

Long sequences of zeros and ones are extremely difficult for humans to understand.

!

Difficult to Maintain

Finding and correcting mistakes in machine code is complicated and time-consuming.

Machine language is also processor dependent. Instructions written for one type of processor may not work on a different processor.

Simple analogy: Machine language is like communicating with a machine using its own native language. The computer understands it perfectly, but humans find it very difficult.

1.2.3 Assembly Language

Writing every instruction using zeros and ones is extremely difficult. Assembly language was developed to make low-level programming slightly easier.

Assembly language uses short symbolic instructions, called mnemonics, instead of binary sequences.

An assembly instruction may look like this: 

MOV AX, 5
ADD AX, 3

Here, words such as MOV and ADD are easier for a programmer to remember than binary instructions.

  • MOV may be used to move or store data.
  • ADD may be used to add values.
  • SUB may be used to subtract values.
  • JMP may be used to move to another instruction.

A computer processor cannot directly execute assembly-language instructions. A translator called an assembler converts assembly language into machine language.

Assembly-language process:
Assembly instructions → Assembler → Machine code → Processor

Assembly language is easier than machine language, but it is still closely connected to the computer's processor, registers, memory, and hardware. Therefore, it is also classified as a low-level language.

1.2.4 High-Level Languages

A high-level language is designed to make programming easier for humans. Its instructions use recognizable words, symbols, and structures instead of long sequences of binary digits.

Examples of high-level programming languages include:

  • Python
  • C
  • C++
  • Java
  • JavaScript
  • Fortran
  • R
  • MATLAB

Programs written in a high-level language cannot usually be executed directly by the processor. They must first be translated into lower-level instructions using a compiler or an interpreter.

High-level-language process:
Human-readable program → Compiler or interpreter → Machine instructions → Processor
R

Readable

The instructions are easier for humans to read and understand.

W

Easier to Write

One high-level instruction may represent several low-level operations.

D

Easier to Debug

Programmers can locate and correct errors more easily.

P

More Portable

Many high-level programs can run on different operating systems with few or no changes.

1.2.5 Is C a Low-Level or High-Level Language?

C is formally classified as a high-level programming language. However, it provides features such as pointers, direct memory access, and efficient hardware interaction.

Because C combines readable programming structures with low-level hardware control, it is sometimes informally called a middle-level language.

Important clarification: The true low-level languages are machine language and assembly language. C is a high-level language with several low-level capabilities.

1.2.6 Where Does Python Belong?

Python is a high-level programming language. It hides most of the complicated details of processor instructions, memory addresses, and hardware operations.

This allows Python programmers to concentrate on the problem they want to solve instead of managing every hardware detail.

Python is considered higher-level than C because Python handles many tasks automatically, including memory management and several low-level operations.

1.2.7 Comparing the Language Levels

Feature Machine Language Assembly Language High-Level Language
Written using Binary digits Mnemonic instructions Human-readable words and symbols
Example 10110000 MOV AX, 5 Python, C, Java
Translator Not required Assembler Compiler or interpreter
Human readability Very difficult Difficult Comparatively easy
Hardware dependence Very high High Comparatively low
In one sentence:
Machine language is easiest for the processor, assembly language is a more readable form of low-level instructions, and high-level languages are designed to make programming easier for humans.

Program, Programming, and Programming Language

These three terms sound similar, but they do not mean exactly the same thing.

1

Program

A program is an ordered collection of instructions written to make a computer perform a particular task.

2

Programming

Programming is the process of understanding a problem, designing a solution, writing instructions, testing them, and correcting mistakes.

3

Programming Language

A programming language is the structured language used to express those instructions.

4

Programmer

A programmer is a person who designs and writes instructions to solve problems using a computer.

A programming language provides:

  • Keywords with predefined meanings
  • Symbols for calculations and comparisons
  • Syntax that determines how instructions must be written
  • Rules that help the computer interpret the instructions
  • Tools for organizing data and solving problems

Questions That May Come to Your Mind

Do I need to install Python 2?
No. Python 2 is old and is no longer supported. This tutorial uses Python 3.
Should I install an alpha or beta version?
No. Select the latest stable version. Alpha and beta versions are mainly intended for testing new features.
My computer already has Python. Should I reinstall it?
First check the installed version. If your computer displays a supported Python 3 version, you usually do not need to reinstall it.
What does “Add Python to PATH” mean?
PATH is like an address book that helps your computer locate programs. If an older Windows installer displays Add Python to PATH, select it.
Should I install Anaconda now?
Not yet. Anaconda can be useful for scientific computing and data science, but the official Python installation is simpler for beginning this course.
Why does macOS or Linux use python3?
On macOS and Linux, the command is commonly written as python3 to clearly indicate that we want to use Python 3.
What if the command says Python was not found?
Close and reopen the terminal first. Windows users can also try py --version. macOS and Linux users should try python3 --version.

3. Python Versions, Implementations, and Libraries

Stage I · Programming and Setup Know Your Python

You have sucessfully installed Python. Do you know which Python?

In the previous lesson, we installed Python. You may now be wondering: Why does my computer show a number such as Python 3.14.8? What is CPython? Why do people talk about NumPy, pandas, PyTorch, or Django?

These names belong to three different ideas: versions, implementations, and libraries. They sound technical, but the difference is simple.

Version

A version tells us which edition or release of Python we are using—for example, Python 3.14.8.

Implementation

An implementation is the actual software engine that reads and runs Python instructions.

Library

A library is a collection of ready-made tools that helps us perform useful tasks without building everything ourselves.

Think of Python as a Car

The version is the model year. The implementation is the engine under the hood. The libraries are additional tools and features such as navigation, sensors, or a music system.

They belong to the same car, but they do different jobs.

What Is a Python Version?

Python continues to improve. Developers fix problems, improve performance, add features, and strengthen security. Each officially released form of Python receives a version number.

A Python version usually contains three numbers:

Interactive Version Decoder

Change the numbers below and observe how a Python version is divided.

.
.

Python 3.14.8

Major version · Minor version · Patch release

3 · Major version

A major generation of the Python language. For beginners today, this will normally be Python 3.

14 · Minor version

A feature release within the same major Python generation.

8 · Patch release

Primarily contains bug corrections and security fixes.

Version numbers change over time

The version displayed above is only an example for learning how Python version numbers work. The newest release changes as Python continues to develop. Always check the official Python website before installing Python.

Which Version Is Installed on My Computer?

python --version
Is the newest version always the best choice?

For a beginner, a current stable Python 3 release is normally a good choice. In research or professional projects, You may need to downgrade python version. Some python packages may not developed or supported in with other library in a latest version. In that case you need to download the lower version which supports all your required libraries.

What Is a Python Implementation?

Python is a language with rules. Those rules describe how Python code should behave. But we still need a real program that reads those instructions and makes the computer perform them.

That program is called a Python implementation. Different implementations can follow the Python language while being designed for different computers or purposes.

Explore Python Implementations

Select an implementation to understand where it is commonly used.

Recommended for this course

CPython

CPython is the standard and most widely used implementation of Python. It is the implementation you normally receive from Python.org.

Best for: beginners, general programming, research, data science, automation, and web development.

Which implementation should you use?

Use CPython. Unless you have a special reason to choose another implementation, you do not need to make any decision. The Python downloaded from Python.org is normally CPython.

What Is a Python Library?

Imagine that you want to draw a graph. You could spend months writing everything required to create axes, colors, labels, lines, and image files or you could use a library whose developers have already built those tools.

A Python library is reusable code written to solve common problems. Libraries are one of the biggest reasons Python is so useful in science, research, artificial intelligence, automation, and web development. Some are alredy available in your current version. You need to install other libraries according to your need.

pip install Library-Name

Standard Library

These tools are included when Python is installed. You do not normally need to download them separately.

Examples: math datetime pathlib json csv

Third-Party Libraries

These libraries are created outside Python's standard library. We install them when a project requires them.

Examples: NumPy pandas Matplotlib PyTorch

Explore Libraries by Purpose

Select the type of work that interests you. You do not need to learn all these libraries.

Module, Package, Library, or Framework?

People sometimes use these words loosely. You do not need to memorize them today, but knowing the basic difference will prevent confusion.

Term Simple meaning Think of it as
Module A single Python file containing reusable code One chapter
Package A collection of related Python modules A book containing chapters
Library A collection of reusable tools for a purpose A bookshelf
Framework A larger structure that guides how an application is built The plan of a building
You do not need to learn every Python library

A researcher studying ocean data may use NumPy, xarray, netCDF4, and Cartopy. A web developer may use Django or FastAPI. A machine learning researcher may use PyTorch. All of them know Python, but their toolboxes are different.

Questions That May Come to Your Mind

Is a Python version the same as an implementation?
No. A version describes a release of the language, such as Python 3.14. An implementation is the program that runs Python, such as CPython or PyPy.
Is Anaconda another Python implementation?
No. Anaconda is a Python distribution. It bundles Python with package-management tools and many libraries commonly used in science and data analysis.
Is Jupyter Notebook a Python implementation?
No. Jupyter is an interactive environment in which you can write and run Python. It normally uses a Python implementation such as CPython underneath.
Will every library work with every Python version?
Not always. A library may need time to support a newly released Python version. This is why researchers sometimes use a slightly older but well-supported Python version.
Is PyPy always faster than CPython?
No. PyPy can make some long-running Python programs faster through just-in-time compilation, but performance depends on the program. Compatibility with some extension libraries can also differ.
Can normal Python code run on MicroPython?
Some code can, but not everything. MicroPython is designed for small devices with limited memory, so it provides a smaller standard library and has some differences from desktop Python.
How many libraries should I learn?
Begin with Python fundamentals. Then learn only the libraries required for your work. Knowing five relevant libraries well is more useful than memorizing the names of one hundred.

4. IDEs: IDLE, VS Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter

Stage I · Programming and Setup Choosing Where to Write Python

Python Is Installed. But Where Do We Write It?

Imagine that you have learned a new language and bought a pen but you still need a comfortable place to write. Python is the language, and the Python interpreter is what understands it. An editor or IDE is the workspace in which we write, organize, run, and correct our instructions.

There is no single “best” Python workspace for everyone. A beginner, a web developer, and a researcher may prefer different tools.

Editor, IDE, or Notebook?

Code Editor

A flexible program for writing code. Additional features can be added using extensions. VS Code belongs mainly to this category.

IDE

An Integrated Development Environment combines an editor, project tools, code assistance, running, and debugging in one application. PyCharm is a full IDE.

Notebook

A notebook divides work into cells and displays code, text, equations, figures, and results together. Jupyter uses this approach.

IDLE Shell
File   Edit   Shell   Debug   Options   Help
Python Shell

Python 3.x.x

Type "help" for more information.

>>>

Learning environment

IDLE

IDLE is Python's simple Integrated Development and Learning Environment. It is usually included with the official Python installation.

  • Simple and lightweight
  • Good for first lessons
  • Includes an editor and Python Shell
  • Limited tools for larger projects
Official Website

Which One Will We Use in This Course?

We will mainly use VS Code because it is flexible, works on Windows, macOS, and Linux, supports both .py and .ipynb files, and can grow with you from beginner projects to research work.

However, you are not forced to use it. The Python language remains the same in IDLE, VS Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter.

Compare the Four Choices

Tool Type Main file Best suited for Setup Computer resources
IDLE Learning environment .py First steps and small programs Usually included Low
VS Code Extensible code editor .py, .ipynb General programming and research Extension required Moderate
PyCharm Full Python IDE .py, .ipynb Large and structured projects Separate installation Moderate to high
JupyterLab Notebook environment .ipynb Data, figures, experiments, and research Package installation Moderate

Help Me Choose

What do you mainly want to do with Python?

Recommended: VS Code

How Do I Get Each One?

IDLE

  1. Search your computer for IDLE.
  2. Open IDLE (Python 3.x).
  3. The first window you see is normally the Python Shell.
  4. Use File → New File to open the editor.

If IDLE is available, no separate download is necessary.

VS Code

  1. Download VS Code from code.visualstudio.com .
  2. Install and open VS Code.
  3. Open the Extensions panel.
  4. Search for Python and install the extension published by Microsoft.
  5. Open the Command Palette and select Python: Select Interpreter.

PyCharm

  1. Visit jetbrains.com/pycharm/download .
  2. Download PyCharm for your operating system.
  3. Install and open the application.
  4. Create a new Python project.
  5. Confirm that PyCharm has selected your installed Python interpreter.

Current PyCharm installations include a Pro trial, after which the core features can continue to be used for free.

JupyterLab

Windows:

python -m pip install jupyterlab

macOS or Linux:

python3 -m pip install jupyterlab

After installation, start it using:

jupyter lab

JupyterLab will normally open inside your web browser.

Installing an IDE Does Not Install Python

An IDE is the workspace. The Python interpreter is the engine that runs the instructions. VS Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter must connect to an installed Python interpreter.

This is why VS Code sometimes displays Select Interpreter. It is asking: “Which installed Python should I use?”

Questions That May Come to Your Mind

Do these tools use different Python languages?
No. The Python language remains the same. These tools provide different ways to write, organize, run, and examine Python instructions.
Is VS Code itself a Python interpreter?
No. VS Code is an editor. You must install Python separately and then select that interpreter inside VS Code.
Is Jupyter an IDE?
Jupyter is more accurately described as an interactive notebook environment. It combines executable cells, formatted text, mathematical equations, figures, and results in one document.
Which one is easiest for a complete beginner?
IDLE is the simplest because it is small and normally included with Python. VS Code requires a little more setup but is more useful as your projects grow.
Which one is best for researchers?
Jupyter is excellent for exploration, figures, equations, and data analysis. VS Code is useful for larger reusable programs. Many researchers use both.
Should I install all four?
No. Begin with one. For this course, VS Code is a good main choice. You can add Jupyter later when you begin working with data and scientific experiments.
Can VS Code open Jupyter notebooks?
Yes. With the appropriate Python and Jupyter extensions, VS Code can open and run .ipynb notebook files.
Is PyCharm free?
PyCharm currently provides core functionality that can continue to be used for free. Some advanced professional features require a paid subscription after the included trial.

5. What are .py file and .ipynb file?

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

You may have noticed that some Python files end with .py, while others end with .ipynb. Both can contain Python code, but they store and present that code in very different ways.

.py
.ipynb

Two containers for Python work

Think about a recipe. You could write the complete recipe on one continuous sheet of paper, or place each step on a separate card with photographs and notes.

A .py file is like the continuous sheet. It is the standard extension for Python source code. The .ipynb is Interactive Python Notebook (Originally stands for IPython Notebook). It is like the collection of cards called cells. It is a file format used by Jupyter Notebook and other interactive computing environments to store and share code, text, and visualizations.

Let us understand both files

.py file

Python source-code file

A .py file is a plain-text file containing Python instructions. It is commonly called a Python script or Python module.

  • Normally runs from top to bottom.
  • Contains code as ordinary readable text.
  • Useful for scripts, applications, automation, and reusable modules.
  • Works well with Git and version control.
  • If there is an error in a .py file, it will be displayed in the terminal when the file is run and ends the execution. After debugging, it will be run again from the beginning.
  • It is time consuming to debug errors in a .py file and rerun the entire file after each fix.

.ipynb file

Jupyter Notebook file

An .ipynb file is an interactive notebook containing cells. A cell can contain code, formatted text, equations, images, or output.

  • Runs one cell at a time.
  • Can save displayed results and figures.
  • Useful for research, teaching, and data exploration.
  • Usually opened with JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, or VS Code.
  • If there is an error in a .ipynb file, You can check cell by cell for errors.
  • It takes less time to debug errors in a .ipynb file as it has memory of the previous executions and doesn't need to rerun the entire file after each fix.
The letters after the final dot are called the file extension. The extension helps your computer understand what kind of file it is and which application may open it.

See the difference

Select a file type to see how the same small analysis might appear inside it.

How does a .py file run?

When Python is asked to run a .py file, the interpreter reads and executes the instructions in the file. Usually, it begins at the top and moves downward.

A Python file named analysis.py can be run from a terminal using: python analysis.py

IDEs such as IDLE, VS Code, and PyCharm can run the same file using a Run button. The button eventually asks a Python interpreter to execute the file.

How does an .ipynb notebook run?

A notebook is divided into cells. Each code cell can be run separately using the run button. Run button attaches to the cell and executes its content. The result normally appears directly below the cell.

Code cell

Contains Python instructions that can be sent to a Python kernel for execution.

Markdown cell

Contains headings, explanations, lists, links, images, or mathematical equations.

Notebook cells can be executed in a different order from their visual order. This is convenient, but it can also cause confusion. When possible, arrange the notebook so it works correctly from the first cell to the last.

What is actually stored inside?

Inside a .py file

A .py file stores ordinary text. If you open it with a text editor, you see the Python instructions directly. 


temperature = 27.5
location = "Kaohsiung"

Inside an .ipynb file

An .ipynb file is a plain-text document structured in JSON format that stores the complete contents, history, and outputs of an interactive computing session. 


{
  "cells": [],
  "metadata": {},
  "nbformat": 4
}
Do not normally edit the raw JSON inside an .ipynb file. Open it using JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, VS Code, or another notebook-compatible application.

Compare .py and .ipynb

Neither format is always better. Each one is designed for a different style of work.

Feature .py .ipynb
Basic structure Continuous text file Collection of interactive cells
Execution Normally runs from top to bottom Cells can be run separately
Explanations Usually written as comments Markdown cells support rich explanations
Saved output Normally not stored inside the file Can store output and figures
Best for Scripts, programs, modules, and automation Research, teaching, and exploration
Version control Simple to compare line by line More difficult because it contains JSON and output
Typical applications IDLE, VS Code, PyCharm JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, VS Code

Check a filename

Enter a filename and let us identify its file type.

Which file should I choose?

Select the type of work you want to do.

In real projects, we often use both

Researchers and data scientists frequently begin with a notebook and later move reusable parts into Python files.

Explore Investigate the data inside an .ipynb notebook.
Organize Identify the steps that should be reused.
Reuse Place reusable functions inside .py files.

Can I convert a file by renaming it?

No. Changing analysis.py to analysis.ipynb does not convert the file into a notebook. The two formats have different internal structures.

Renaming a file extension changes its name, not its internal format. Use an export or conversion tool when you genuinely need to convert between formats.

Quick questions

Does an .ipynb file contain Python only?

No. A notebook can contain Python code, Markdown text, equations, images, metadata, and stored output. Jupyter also supports kernels for some other programming languages.

Can VS Code open both file types?

Yes. VS Code can open .py files using its Python support. It can also open .ipynb notebooks when the required Python and Jupyter extensions are installed.

Is a notebook better than a Python file?

Not always. A notebook is excellent for exploration and explanation. A Python file is generally better for reusable scripts, modules, applications, and automated workflows.

Why does a notebook remember my figures?

Notebook output can be stored inside the .ipynb file. That output may include text, tables, images, and visualizations.

Can one project contain both formats?

Yes. A project can use notebooks for exploration and presentation while keeping reusable calculations and functions inside Python files.

6. Terminal Basics: Command prompt, PowerShell, and Shell

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

The terminal may look like a frightening black window filled with unfamiliar text. But it is simply another way to talk to your computer that is one short command at a time.

C:\Users\Learner> python --version
Python 3.x.x

C:\Users\Learner> _

The black window should not be not that scary to you.

When we use buttons and menus, we communicate with the computer through a graphical interface. In a terminal, we communicate by typing short text instructions.

The terminal is not only for expert programmers. We will use it for simple tasks such as checking Python, moving between folders, installing libraries, and running files.

Terminal and shell are not exactly the same

People often use the words interchangeably, but they describe different parts of the command-line experience.

Terminal

The terminal is the visible application or window. It displays text, accepts keyboard input, and shows the result of a command.

Shell

The shell works inside the terminal. It reads your command, interprets it, and asks the operating system or another program to perform the task.

Think of the terminal as a conversation window and the shell as the interpreter listening inside that window.

Which terminal or shell do I have?

The tools available to you depend mainly on your operating system.

Command Prompt

Command Prompt uses the traditional Windows command interpreter called cmd.exe. It supports commands such as dir, cd, and cls.

Windows

PowerShell

PowerShell is a newer command-line shell and scripting environment. It provides commands called cmdlets, such as Get-Location and Get-ChildItem.

Windows and cross-platform

Bash or Zsh

Bash and Zsh are common Unix-style shells. Bash is widely used on Linux, while modern macOS systems use Zsh as the default login shell.

Linux and macOS

What is the prompt?

The prompt is the text shown before the place where you type. It often displays your username, computer name, or current folder.

Command Prompt

C:\Users\Learner>

PowerShell

PS C:\Users\Learner>

Bash

learner@computer:~$
Do not type the prompt symbols shown in tutorials. If a tutorial displays $ python3 --version, type only python3 --version. The $ represents the prompt.

Safe Terminal Simulator

Select a shell and try the suggested commands. This is only a webpage simulation—it will not change anything on your computer.

Command Prompt — Safe Simulation

Anatomy of a command

A command can contain a program name, an option, and an argument. Not every command requires all three.

python Program
+
-m Option
+
pip Argument
+
--version Additional argument
The complete command is python -m pip --version. It asks your selected Python interpreter to open the pip module and display its version.

Essential commands for beginners

Different shells sometimes use different commands for the same task.

Task Command Prompt PowerShell Bash / Zsh
Show current folder cd Get-Location pwd
List files and folders dir Get-ChildItem ls
Enter a folder cd folder cd folder cd folder
Move to parent folder cd .. cd .. cd ..
Create a folder mkdir folder mkdir folder mkdir folder
Clear the screen cls Clear-Host clear
Check Python py --version python --version python3 --version
Leave the shell exit exit exit

Understanding paths

A path describes the location of a file or folder on your computer.

Windows path

C:\Users\Haripriya\python-learning

Windows paths normally use backslashes (\).

Linux or macOS path

/home/haripriya/python-learning

Unix-style paths use forward slashes (/).

If a folder name contains spaces, place the path inside quotation marks. For example: cd "Python Projects".

Terminal safety

A terminal is powerful because commands can make changes quickly. That power should be used carefully.

Never paste an unfamiliar command into your terminal without understanding what it does. Some commands can delete files, modify your system, or install unwanted software.
  • Read a command completely before pressing Enter.
  • Check your current folder before moving, renaming, or deleting anything.
  • Avoid using administrator or root privileges unless the task genuinely requires them.
  • Do not share passwords, access tokens, or private keys shown in a terminal.
  • When learning, practise inside a separate test folder.

Beginner terminal practice

Complete these steps using the terminal on your computer. They do not delete or overwrite any files.

  1. Open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or your IDE's integrated terminal.
  2. Display your current folder using cd, Get-Location, or pwd.
  3. List the files in that folder using dir, Get-ChildItem, or ls.
  4. Create a folder using mkdir python-learning.
  5. Enter it using cd python-learning.
  6. Check your Python installation using py --version, python --version, or python3 --version.

Quick questions

Is the terminal the same as Python?

No. The terminal provides a place to enter commands. Python is a separate program that can be started from the terminal.

Is PowerShell the same as Command Prompt?

No. Both are available on Windows, but they are different shells. PowerShell provides its own cmdlets and more advanced scripting capabilities.

Why does one tutorial use python and another use python3?

The command depends on the operating system and how Python was installed. Windows often supports py or python, while Linux and macOS commonly use python3.

Can I use the terminal inside VS Code?

Yes. VS Code has an integrated terminal. Depending on your system and settings, it may open PowerShell, Command Prompt, Bash, Zsh, or another installed shell.

Will closing the terminal delete my files?

No. Closing a normal terminal window ends that terminal session, but files already saved on your computer remain there.

Do I need to memorize every command?

No. Begin with a few commands such as cd, ls or dir, mkdir, and the Python version command. Repeated use will gradually make them familiar.

7. How to write and compile code using code editor?

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

Python is installed, your editor is ready, and you understand the terminal. Now it is time to create a real Python file, write your first instructions, and ask Python to run them.

# first_program.py
print( "Hello, Python!" )

Output:
Hello, Python!

Your first complete coding workflow

Writing code is only one part of programming. We also need to save the code inside a file, choose the correct Python interpreter, run the file, and examine the output.

We will demonstrate this workflow using VS Code. The same basic process also applies to IDLE, PyCharm, and other Python editors.

Before we begin

Three separate components work together when you run Python code in VS Code.

Python The interpreter that reads and executes your Python instructions.
VS Code The editor where you create, organize, and view your files.
Python extension Connects VS Code with Python and adds Python-specific tools.

Write and run your first Python file

Follow each step carefully. Small details such as the folder, filename, and selected interpreter are important.

1

Create a project folder

Create a folder named python-learning. This folder will contain the files created during this course.

You can create it using your file manager or the terminal:

mkdir python-learning
2

Open the folder in VS Code

Open VS Code and select:

File → Open Folder → python-learning

Opening a folder creates a workspace. New files will appear inside the Explorer panel.

3

Create a Python file

Select the New File button in the Explorer panel and name the file:

first_program.py

The .py extension tells VS Code that this is a Python source file.

4

Select the Python interpreter

Open the Command Palette using Ctrl + Shift + P. On macOS, use Command + Shift + P.

Search for:

Python: Select Interpreter

Select the Python installation you installed earlier.

5

Write the Python instruction

Type the following line inside first_program.py:

first_program.py
print( "Hello, Python!" )

The print() instruction asks Python to display something on the screen.

6

Save the file

Press Ctrl + S on Windows or Linux. On macOS, press Command + S.

A small dot beside the filename usually indicates that the file contains unsaved changes.

7

Run the file

Select the triangular Run Python File button near the upper-right corner of the editor.

VS Code opens its integrated terminal and asks the selected Python interpreter to run the file.

Hello, Python!

Are we compiling or running Python?

In languages such as C or C++, programmers normally perform a separate compilation step that creates an executable file. Python usually hides this step from the beginner.

Source code You write instructions inside a .py file.
Python interpreter Python reads and checks your source code.
Bytecode Python internally compiles the code into intermediate instructions.
Result Python executes the instructions and displays the output.
In daily Python work, simply say “run the Python file.” Python handles its internal bytecode compilation automatically.

Three ways to run a Python file

These methods run the same file using the selected Python interpreter.

Run button

Select the triangular Run Python File button in the upper-right corner of VS Code.

Run Python File

Right-click

Right-click inside the editor and select the Python run option.

Run Python File in Terminal

Terminal

Open the terminal in the folder containing your Python file and enter a command.

python first_program.py
On Windows, you may need py first_program.py. On Linux or macOS, you may need python3 first_program.py.

Mini Code Editor

Edit the message and press Run. This is a safe browser simulation of a small part of Python—it does not execute code on your computer.

first_program.py Saved
1 2
Terminal output
Press “Run Code” to see the output.
This educational simulator supports simple variable assignments and print(). Use VS Code, IDLE, PyCharm, or Jupyter to run complete Python code.

Choose a good filename

A clear filename makes your project easier to understand and avoids several common problems.

Good filenames

  • first_program.py
  • temperature_analysis.py
  • student_results.py
  • plot_velocity.py

Avoid these names

  • my program.py — contains a space
  • 1program.py — begins with a number
  • python.py — may cause confusion
  • numpy.py — may hide the real library
Use lowercase descriptive words separated by underscores. Always keep the .py extension for a Python source file.

Useful VS Code shortcuts

Action Windows/Linux macOS
Save file Ctrl + S Command + S
Command Palette Ctrl + Shift + P Command + Shift + P
Open terminal Ctrl + ` Control + `
Find text Ctrl + F Command + F
Comment or uncomment Ctrl + / Command + /

Common problems

The Run button is missing

Confirm that the file ends with .py and that the Microsoft Python extension is installed and enabled in VS Code.

VS Code says Python is not found

Open the Command Palette, select Python: Select Interpreter, and choose your installed Python version. If Python was installed while VS Code was open, restart VS Code.

The terminal says the file does not exist

The terminal may be in a different folder. Use dir or ls to check whether the Python file is present in the current folder.

My latest changes do not appear in the output

Save the file before running it. Press Ctrl + S or Command + S, then run the file again.

I see a red error message

Read the final line of the error first. Check the filename, quotation marks, parentheses, spelling, and indentation. Errors are part of programming and usually tell us where to begin investigating.

The output appears in a different panel

Make sure you selected Run Python File in Terminal. Some extensions may send output to an Output panel or Debug Console instead.

Your first practical task

Complete these steps using your actual code editor.

  1. Open the python-learning folder in VS Code.
  2. Create a file named about_me.py.
  3. Use print() to display your name.
  4. Add another print() instruction describing why you want to learn Python.
  5. Save and run the file using the Run button.
  6. Run the same file from the integrated terminal.
  7. Deliberately remove one quotation mark, run the file, and observe the error. Then repair it.

What did we learn?

  • Open a project folder before creating Python files.
  • Python source filenames end with .py.
  • VS Code needs the Python extension and a selected interpreter.
  • Save the file before running it.
  • A Python file can be run using the editor's Run button or a terminal command.
  • Python internally compiles source code into bytecode.
  • We normally say “run the Python file” because Python handles the internal compilation automatically.
  • Program output and error messages appear in the terminal.

Quick questions

Do I need to compile a Python file before every run?

No. In normal Python development, you run the source file directly. Python automatically performs the necessary internal bytecode compilation.

What is the difference between VS Code and Python?

VS Code is the editor where you write and organize code. Python is the interpreter that executes the instructions.

Why must the file end with .py?

The extension identifies it as a Python source file. It helps the editor provide Python syntax coloring, suggestions, formatting, and appropriate run options.

Can I run the same file without VS Code?

Yes. A saved Python file can be run from Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, IDLE, PyCharm, or another Python-compatible environment.

What is a .pyc file?

It is a cached bytecode file that Python may create automatically. Beginners normally do not need to open, edit, or create it manually.

8. VS Code Tutorial for Python

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

VS Code may initially look like an aeroplane cockpit: buttons, panels, icons, and menus everywhere. You do not need to learn everything at once. Let us understand only the tools needed for writing Python.

What makes VS Code useful?

Visual Studio Code is a flexible code editor. You can use it to write C++ code, Python code, or other programming languages like html, CSS, java script. In this tutorial we will focus on using VS Code for Python development. By itself, it is not Python and does not include a Python interpreter.

We need to add the Python extension for VS Code to provide full Python development support. After adding the Python extension, VS Code can help us write, run, organize, inspect, and debug Python programs. The same editor can later support Jupyter notebooks, Git, remote servers, and many other programming languages.

Explore the VS Code interface

Step 1: Add the Python extensions

VS Code is a general code editor. An extension teaches it how to provide tools for a particular language or type of work. Follow the four illustrated steps below before writing code.

Your goal: install the official Python extension. Also install Jupyter if you will use .ipynb notebooks in this course.

Open the Extensions view

  1. Open VS Code.
  2. Find the four-block icon on the Activity Bar at the left.
  3. Click it once.

Shortcut: press Ctrl + Shift + X on Windows/Linux or Command + Shift + X on macOS.

Search for the official Python extension

  1. Click the search box at the top.
  2. Enter the exact extension ID ms-python.python.

Searching by the exact ID helps you avoid choosing a different extension with a similar name.

Check the publisher and install

  2. Confirm that the publisher is Microsoft.

  4. Wait until the Install button disappears or changes to management buttons such as Disable or Uninstall.

VS Code may also add supporting Microsoft extensions such as Pylance and Python Debugger.

Add Jupyter for notebook files

  1. Return to the Extensions search box.
  2. Search for ms-toolsai.jupyter.
  3. Choose Jupyter published by Microsoft.
  4. Click Install.

Jupyter is needed for the notebook lessons that use .ipynb files. It is not required merely to run ordinary .py files.

Quick questions

Does VS Code install Python automatically?

No. VS Code, the Python extension, and the Python interpreter are separate components. Python must be installed and then selected inside VS Code.

Do I need the Code Runner extension?

What does the selected interpreter control?

What is the Command Palette?

Is a breakpoint an error?

No. A breakpoint is a debugging marker that deliberately pauses the program so you can inspect its current state.

9. The python interpreters and your first program

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

We have prepared our computer, explored the terminal, and learned how to use VS Code. Now we are finally ready to give Python an instruction and watch the computer follow it.

Python Code → Result

What is the Python interpreter?

You write Python instructions in a language that humans can read. However, the computer's processor does not directly understand those instructions.

The Python interpreter is the program that reads your Python code, checks it, translates it into instructions Python can execute, and produces a result.

Two ways to use the Python interpreter

Python can execute instructions interactively or read them from a saved Python file.

How to open interactive Python

Open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or the integrated terminal in VS Code. Then enter the command appropriate for your system.

Windows

py

The Python launcher commonly used on Windows.

Windows alternative

python

Works when Python is available through your system path.

Linux or macOS

python3

Common command for starting Python 3 on Unix-style systems.

When interactive Python starts, you normally see >>>. This is the Python prompt. It means that Python is waiting for your instruction.
Do not type the >>> symbol when copying an example from a tutorial. It represents the interpreter prompt, not part of the Python instruction.

Your first Python program

Open python in interactive mode or VS code. Then type the following instructions. You should see the same output as shown below.

first_program.py
1 # My first Python program
2 print( "Hello, Python!" )
3 print( "I have written my first program." )
4 print( "I will learn one step at a time." )

Save the file and select Run Python File. You should see:

Terminal output
Hello, Python!
I have written my first program.
I will learn one step at a time.

Try your first program

Change the messages and select Run. This is a safe webpage simulation supporting simple print() instructions. Remember that if you are printing a message keep it inside quotation marks. We will learn more about quotation marks in the upcoming lessons.

first_program.py
Program output
Select “Run Program” to see the output.
This simulator does not execute real Python. Use VS Code, IDLE, PyCharm, or Jupyter when experimenting with complete Python programs.
I hope you have installed python and VS-code in your system by now. Now open a new .ipynb file and open code and write every code given in the tutorial after saving the file. Check the outputs. Try to play with code and see how it works. If you get an error now then congratulations you have started your python journey! Errors are part of programming. Try to find the error and correct it."

Quick questions

Is the Python interpreter the same as VS Code?

No. VS Code is an editor. The Python interpreter is the program that actually executes Python instructions.

What does >>> mean?

It is Python's primary interactive prompt. It means the interpreter is waiting for the next instruction.

Should I type >>> before every command?

No. Python displays that prompt automatically in interactive mode. It should not be copied into a .py file.

What is the difference between interactive and script mode?

Interactive mode executes one instruction immediately. Script mode executes instructions saved inside a Python source file.

Why do we place text inside quotation marks?

Quotation marks tell Python that the enclosed characters are literal text rather than the name of a variable or another Python instruction.

How do I leave interactive Python?

Enter exit() and press Enter. Keyboard shortcuts for ending the session also exist, but exit() is clear and easy for beginners.

10. Important Things to Know Before Programming

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

Before writing large programs, learn these small rules. Most beginner errors happen because of one missing letter, space, file, or symbol—not because Python is difficult.

Remember: Python follows instructions exactly. It cannot guess what we mean, so we must write clearly.
1

File Paths and Folders

A file path tells Python where a file is stored on your computer. Beginners often see an error simply because Python is looking in the wrong folder. You can simply copy the file by "ctrl+c" and paste into VS-code "Code editor" by "ctrl+v". It will automatically set the path for you.

data/temperature.csv

General Practice: Keep your data inside your project folder whenever possible. Then use a simple relative path such as data/temperature.csv.

2

Python Is Case-Sensitive

Capital and small letters are different in Python. print, Print, and PRINT are not the same instruction.

print("Hello")
Print("Hello")

Write Python keywords exactly as shown in examples.

3

Indentation Matters

In Python, indentation refers to the whitespaces (spaces or tabs) added at the beginning of a line of code. You can't write one line from starting of the row and the next line with some spaces.

print("Hello")
    print("It is hot")

This is wrong indentation. The second line should not have spaces before it. It should be like this:

print("Hello")
print("It is hot")

We will learn more about indentation: where to use spaces and tabs in the upcoming lessons.

4

Save Files with the Correct Extension

The end of a filename tells VS Code what type of file it is. Python programs should normally end with .py.

my_first_program.py
my_first_program.ipynb
my_first_program
my_first_program.txt

Jupyter Notebook projects use the extension .ipynb.

5

Symbols Must Match

Python notices missing quotation marks, brackets, parentheses, and colons. Check that every opening symbol has a closing partner.

Rule of thumb: If you open a symbol, you must close it. If you start a string with a quotation mark, you must end it with the same type of quotation mark. This will prevent syntax errors.
print("Hello")
print("Hello)
print("Hello"
print("Hello')

When an error appears, first check quotation marks, parentheses, square brackets, and colons.

The five beginner checks

Before running your program, check the file path, capital letters, indentation, file extension, and matching symbols.

Questions That May Come to Your Mind

How to give the indent correct?
In Vs- code one you go to next line by pressing "Enter" key, it will automatically give the correct indent. If you want to remove the indent, you can use "Backspace" key.
Will my code work if my file and data are in different folders?
Yes. You can use the full path of the data file in your code. For example, if your data file is in "C:\Users\YourName\Documents\data\temperature.csv", you can use that full path in your code. However, it is recommended to keep your data file in the same folder as your code file or in a subfolder to avoid confusion.
Are the word messages "Hello" and "hello" different in python?
Yes. In Python, strings are case-sensitive, so "Hello" and "hello" are treated as different strings. But if you are using them in print statements, they will both be printed as they are. For example, print("Hello") will print Hello and print("hello") will print hello.

10. Important things to know about before programming

Stage I · Programming and SetupPlanned

Every programmer sees errors—even people who have been programming for twenty years. An error does not mean that you have failed. It means that your program has given you a clue about what needs attention.

Errors are messages, not monsters

When a Python instruction cannot be understood or completed, Python displays an error message. The message usually tells us what kind of problem occurred and where Python noticed it.

Learning programming does not mean learning how to avoid every error. It means learning how to read, investigate, and correct errors.

The normal programming journey

Programming is usually a repeated process rather than a straight path from code to success.

Write Write an instruction based on your current idea.
Run Ask Python to execute the instructions.
Investigate Read the output or error message carefully.
Improve Correct the problem and run the program again.
The goal is not to write perfect code on the first attempt. The goal is to make each attempt teach you something useful.

Three different kinds of problems

Beginners often call every problem an “error,” but it helps to separate them into three broad groups.

Syntax error

Python cannot understand the structure of the instruction. A quote, parenthesis, colon, or another required symbol may be missing.

Exception

The instruction is structurally valid, but a problem occurs while Python is executing it, such as dividing by zero or using an undefined name.

Logic error or bug

The program runs without displaying an error, but the result is incorrect because the instructions do not represent the intended logic.

How to read a traceback

A traceback is the report Python displays when an unhandled exception stops the program.

Python traceback
Traceback (most recent call last): File "first_program.py", line 3, in <module> print(student_name) ^^^^^^^^^^^^ NameError: name 'student_name' is not defined
1 Read the last line first

The final line gives the error type and a short explanation: NameError.

2 Find the file and line

Python reports the filename and line number where the problem was noticed.

3 Inspect the instruction

Examine the displayed code and nearby lines. The real cause may appear just before the highlighted position.

The highlighted position shows where Python noticed the problem. The actual mistake may be slightly earlier, such as an unclosed quotation mark or parenthesis.

Error Detective

Select an error type. Read the broken code and traceback before revealing the correction.

                    Traceback

            When an error appears, avoid changing many unrelated lines.
            Use a small, repeatable investigation process.
        


        
    

            
  1. 
                Stop and read the message instead of immediately closing
                the terminal.
            
    2. 

            
  2.

                message.
            
    3. 

            
  3. 
                Find the filename and line number mentioned in the
                traceback.
            
    4.

    5.

                parentheses, and indentation.
            
    6. 

            
  6. 
                Correct one likely cause at a time.
            
    7.

                If the problem remains, search using the error type and
                the important part of the message.
            
    9. 

        


    



    
    


        

            
            The most difficult error may show no red message
        


        

            A logic error occurs when the program runs but produces an
            incorrect answer.
        


        


            


                
Incorrect logic


                
total = 100
students = 4

average = total * students

print(average)


                

                    Output: 400
                


            


            

            


                
Corrected logic


                
total = 100
students = 4

average = total / students

print(average)


                

                    Output: 25.0
                


            


        


        


            

            

                Python cannot know that you intended to calculate an
                average. Both multiplication and division are valid
                operations. We must check whether the result makes sense.
            


        


    



    
    


        

            
            A programmer's mindset
        


        

            “An error is not Python rejecting you. It is Python showing
            you the first place where the conversation became unclear.”
        


        


            

            

                Experienced programmers are not people who never make
                errors. They are people who have practised investigating
                errors without panicking.
            


        


    



    
    


        

            
            Modify and investigate

    4. 

            
  4. 
                Change print to Print and
                identify the error type.
            
    5.

                Try print(10 / 0) and examine the traceback.
            
    6.

                Write down the filename, line number, error type, and

    7.

                disappears.

    9. 
        


    



    
    


        

            
            What did we learn?
        


        
    
            
  • 
                Errors are a normal part of programming.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                A syntax error means Python cannot understand the code's
                structure.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                An exception occurs while valid Python code is being
                executed.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                A logic error produces an incorrect result without
                necessarily displaying an error message.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                A traceback reports the execution path, filename, line,
                error type, and message.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                The final traceback line is often the best place to begin
                reading.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                Correct one likely problem at a time and rerun the
                program.
            
    • 

            
  • 
                Error-solving improves through practice.
            
    • 
        


    


    
    
    


        

            
            Quick questions
        


        

            
                Does an error mean I am bad at programming?
            

            

                No. Errors occur during ordinary programming work at
                every experience level. Your skill is demonstrated by how
                you investigate and learn from them.
            

        


        

            
                Should I read a traceback from the top or bottom?
            

            

                For a beginner, the final line is often the best starting
                point because it gives the error type and message. Then
                move upward to find the filename, line number, and code.
            

        


        

            
                Is every error a syntax error?
            

            

                No. Syntax errors occur when Python cannot parse the code.
                Other problems occur during execution and are called
                exceptions.
            

        


        

            
                Why does Python point to the wrong place?
            

            

                Python usually points to the place where it noticed that
                something was wrong. The actual cause may appear earlier,
                such as an unclosed quote or parenthesis on the previous
                line.
            

        


        

            
                Why do some incorrect programs show no error?
            

            

                Python checks whether an instruction is valid, but it does
                not always know your intention. Valid instructions can
                still represent the wrong calculation or logic.
            

        


        

            
                Should I copy the entire error into a search engine?
            

            

                Usually, search for the error type and the most important
                part of the final message. Remove personal paths,
                usernames, passwords, tokens, and confidential project
                information before sharing an error online.
            

        


    



    
    


        

        

    





11. Variables, Assignment, and Naming Rules
Stage II · Core PythonPlanned


        

            All programs store everything in variables. Think of a variable as a container that holds a value. Whatever you put in the variable stored in that variable.But if you put a new value in the variable, it will replace the old value. 
            If you organise the files or your belongings properly with labels, you can find them easily. You don't need to remember where you put each item. So most of time we label on medicines, food items and necessary things. A person/ student can 
            finish daily life work much faster ifhe/she is organised properly.
            Computer is considered as most perfect tool. It can't store anything without labelling. The variable name is like a label on the container.
        

    

    
    

        

            

                21
            

        


        

            
Every container should have a label to identify it


            

                Suppose you have a box containing the number 21.
                To find it again, you attach the label age to
                the box.
            


            
In Python, we can write this as:


            

                age =
                21
            


            

                Here, age is the variable name and
                21 is the value assigned to it.
            

        

    


    
    

        

            
            What is a variable?
        


        

            A variable is a name that refers to a value in a
            program. We use that name whenever we want to work with the value.
        


        

            student_name =
            "Ananya"


            age =
            21


            temperature =
            27.5


            is_beginner =
            True
        


        

            Python understands the type of each value automatically. We do not
            have to declare whether a variable contains text, a whole number,
            a decimal number, or a Boolean value.
        

    

    

        

            
            Types of variables?
        


        

            integer_var =
            only integer numbers


            float_var =
            Any decimal number, it can include integer in form of 22.0


            character =
            a single character


            string_var =
            a sequence of characters

            boolean_var =
            True or False

        

    


    
    

        

            
            What does assignment mean?
        


        

            The = symbol is called the
            assignment operator. It assigns the value on its
            right to the variable name on its left.
        


        

            

                score
                The variable name
            


            

                
            


            

                85
                The value being assigned
            

        


        

            score =
            85
        


        

            

            

                Assignment operator reads the statement from right to left: It 
                “take the value 85 and assign it to score.”
                In Python, = means assignment. Don't confused it with "is equal to"
                in the mathematical sense. For integer, float and boolean values, we can write the number or True/False after "=" sign. But in case of strings and characters, we need to use quotes. If you use a=Roy. 
                Then Python will think that Roy is a variable name and we need to assign the value of Roy to a. But if you use a="Roy" or a='Roy', then Python will understand that Roy is a string value.
            

        

    



    
    

        

            
            Variables can be changed
        


        

            The name “variable” tells us that its value can vary or change
            while the program is running.
        


        

            score =
            50

            # score currently contains 50



            score =
            80

            # the old value is replaced by 80



            print(score)

            # Output: 80
        


        

            
            

                Assigning a new value to the same variable makes the variable
                refer to the new value.
            

        

    


    
    

        

            
            Variables in real programs
        


        

            

                
Student information

                student_name = "Ravi"
            


            

                
Research data

                sample_temperature = 18.7
            


            

                
Online shopping

                product_price = 499
            


            

                
Login status

                is_logged_in = False
            

        

    


    
    

        

            
            Try it: Create a variable
        


        

            Enter a variable name and a value. This activity will show how the
            assignment looks in Python.
        


        

            

                
                
            


            

                
                
            


            
        


        

    


    
    

        

            
            Rules for naming variables
        


        

            We can choose variable names, but Python requires us to follow a
            few rules.
        


        

            

                
                    
                

                

                    Start with a letter or underscore
                    

                        age and _result are valid.
                        2age is not valid.
                    

                

            


            

                
                    
                

                

                    Letters, numbers, and underscores
                    

                        After the first character, names may contain letters,
                        digits, and underscores.
                    

                

            


            

                
                    
                

                

                    No spaces or hyphens
                    

                        Use student_name, not
                        student name or student-name.
                    

                

            


            

                
                    
                

                

                    Do not use Python keywords
                    

                        Names such as if, for,
                        class, and True have special
                        meanings in Python.
                    

                

            


            

                
                    
                

                

                    Names are case-sensitive
                    

                        score, Score, and
                        SCORE are three different names.
                    

                

            


            

                
                    
                

                

                    Use meaningful names
                    

                        water_temperature is clearer than
                        x when storing water temperature.
                    

                

            

        

    


    
    

        

            
            Good names make code easier to understand
        


        

            
                

                    Avoid
                    Better name
                    Why?
                

            

            
                

                    n
                    student_name
                    Explains what the text represents.
                


                

                    x1
                    sample_count
                    Describes the stored number.
                


                

                    temp
                    water_temperature
                    Removes confusion about which temperature.
                


                

                    p
                    product_price
                    Makes the program readable.
                

            
        


        

            

            

                Python programmers normally write variable names using
                snake_case: lowercase words separated by
                underscores, such as student_name.
            

        

    


    
    

        

            
            A name that should not change
        


        

            Sometimes we store a value that should remain unchanged. Python
            does not lock the value, but programmers write its name in capital
            letters as a warning.
        


        

            PI =
            3.14159


            MAX_STUDENTS =
            50


            UNIVERSITY_NAME =
            "ABC University"
        


        

            These are called constants by convention. Python
            can still change them, but their capitalized names tell other
            programmers that they should not be changed.
        

    


    
    

        

            
            Variable Name Checker
